title: Mitigating Social Bias in Large Language Models: A Multi-Objective Approach Within a Multi-Agent Framework
findings: The paper's proposed method, MOMA, successfully reduces social bias across nine categories, including religion, on the BBQ and StereoSet benchmarks. While aggregate results show significant bias score reduction (e.g., icat score enhanced by up to 58.1%), the paper does not provide a separate analysis or specific quantitative findings for the religion category alone.

measurement_description: The benchmarks (BBQ, StereoSet) measure social bias and stereotypes across nine topics, one of which is Religion. For BBQ, this is done via multiple-choice questions reflecting bias, while StereoSet uses intrasentence (fill-in-the-blank) and intersentence (predicting the next sentence) tasks with stereotypical, anti-stereotypical, and unrelated options.
